entries.description: reserve() reads stock, awaits, then writes an absolute value without the SKU lock that restock/release take, so concurrent reservations oversell the last units (lost update).
reserve() only checks that quantity is an integer; a negative quantity passes the stock check and increases available stock (restock rejects <= 0, reserve does not).
place() calls inventory.reserve() without await: out-of-stock never reaches the catch, the order is marked reserved regardless, and the rejection is unhandled.
listForCustomer() slices to start + pageSize - 1 (slice's end is already exclusive), so every page silently drops its last order.
The cache key is only the SKU, not the currency: a EUR checkout after a USD one is served the USD quote (wrong price and currency).
expiresAt adds ttlSeconds to a millisecond clock, so quotes expire after 300 ms instead of 5 minutes and the cache barely caches (and always takes the soft-refresh path).

When every capture attempt throws, the errors are only logged and result stays undefined; the code falls through and records a captured payment under a fresh id, so the order is marked paid without being charged.
refund() compares the request with capturedCents instead of what is left (capturedCents - refundedCents), so repeated partial refunds can refund more than was captured.
pump() checks active < concurrency but run() only increments active after awaiting the journal write, so one pump starts every due job at once and exceeds the concurrency limit.

If journal.delete/put or onDead throws inside the outcome handlers, active is never decremented and pump never runs again (no finally); the voided promise rejects unhandled and the queue permanently loses a slot.
The limit query parameter is passed to listForCustomer unchecked: limit=1000000 returns everything, limit=0 or negative gives wrong pages, and a non-number gives NaN and an empty page.

entries.description: RateLimiter never removes keys: every distinct client IP keeps an entry (even an empty list) forever, so memory grows without bound.
allocate() loops with index <= parts - 1, which is the same as index < parts; the shares are correct.
void this.refresh(...) is a deliberate background refresh; refresh() catches its own errors, so nothing is unhandled.
reservation == null deliberately covers both null and undefined; it is not a loose-equality bug.

matching: A target is credited to an entry only when it names the entry's file, its lines overlap the entry's range (within 3 lines), and its title or detail contains at least one of the entry's evidence terms. Several entries qualifying equally is ambiguous; a file-and-evidence match without overlapping lines, or file-and-lines without evidence, is weak. Ambiguous and weak targets are listed for adjudication, never credited.
